sermon.title: Suppressing the Spirit: July 4, 2020
sermon.speaker: Unidentified speaker (not clearly Pastor Kincer)
sermon.summary: On Independence Day weekend, this message compares a king who refused just laws to people who suppress the Spirit. Herod knew John was holy yet killed him; Zedekiah caved but Ebed-Melech rescued Jeremiah; Stephen’s hearers always resisted the Spirit. The church must put away malice, assemble, not quench the Spirit, and speak truth.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear.

faqs.question: What happened on July 4, 1776?
faqs.answer: The founding fathers signed the Declaration of Independence.

faqs.question: What did the princes do to Jeremiah?
faqs.answer: They cast him into a dungeon with no water, and he sank in the mire.

faqs.question: Who was Ebed-Melech?
faqs.answer: Mentioned only in this story; God had a special message and reward for him in Jeremiah 39:16.

faqs.question: Whom does God use?
faqs.answer: His people — Ebed-Melech, Stephen, Paul and Peter fought for the Spirit of God though suppressed.

faqs.question: Did John know who he was?
